pinterest.title: Chinese Wedding Traditions: Betrothal Gifts, Hair Combing and the Tea Ceremony
pinterest.description: Chinese wedding traditions follow a sequence, and they differ by dialect group, region and family. In Singapore, most Chinese weddings begin with guo da li, betrothal gifts carried to the bride's family on an auspicious day. Then come hair combing the night before, door games at the bride's home and the tea ceremony, held at the groom's home and again at the bride's. Our guide walks each rite in wedding order, for couples planning in China or at home in Australia.

pinterest.title: The Chinese Hair-Combing Ceremony: What Happens the Night Before the Wedding
pinterest.description: Singapore's National Heritage Board describes shang tou, a hair-combing ritual on the night before a Chinese wedding. In both homes, the bride and the groom each face a pair of lighted candles while a woman of good fortune combs the hair four times, repeating an auspicious phrase each time. Traditionally a Cantonese custom, it is also practised by other dialect groups in Singapore. Decide early who will hold the comb. More Chinese wedding traditions in our guide.

pinterest.title: Chinese Wedding Tea Ceremony: Who Serves Whom, and in What Order
pinterest.description: In Singapore, the Chinese wedding tea ceremony is held at the groom's home and again at the bride's. Tea is offered first to the gods, then the groom's ancestors, his parents, then senior family members and other relatives. The couple kneel, or bow if they prefer, and offer each cup with both hands. The tea is usually brewed with lotus seeds, red dates and longans. Agree the list of elders in advance. Read the step-by-step guide.

slides: Chinese wedding traditions you did not know, in the order they happen
There is no single traditional Chinese wedding. Cantonese, Hokkien, Teochew and other families each keep their own versions.
Betrothal gifts (guo da li): in Singapore, most Chinese weddings begin with gifts carried to the bride's family two to four weeks ahead, on an auspicious day.
Gifts carry meaning: mandarin oranges for good luck, charcoal for a good life after marriage. The bride's family returns some to show they accept the marriage.
Hair combing (shang tou): the night before, in both homes, a woman of good fortune combs the hair four times, repeating an auspicious phrase each time.
Door games: in Singapore, the bride's "sisters" hold the door until the groom and his groomsmen meet their playful demands, a red packet included.
The tea ceremony: in Singapore it is held at the groom's home and again at the bride's. The couple kneel or bow and offer tea to elders with both hands, in order of seniority.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Chinese wedding traditions are usually presented as a list of curiosities. In a family, they are a sequence.

Gifts carried to the bride's home weeks ahead. A comb drawn through the hair by candlelight. A door that only opens once the groom has earned it. Cups of tea offered on bended knee.

Customs differ by dialect group, region and family, so many of the details in our guide come from Singapore's heritage bodies and describe Chinese weddings there, not every Chinese family. Ask both families which rites they expect before you set the day's order.

Which of these did your parents keep? Tell us in the comments.
